candidates.source_name: Finančná správa SR — Open Data portál (ODFS), kategória eKasa / e-cash register
candidates.why_relevant: Single most valuable non-central-bank source in this cell: ~10 recurring datasets from the eKasa online cash-register system — počet vytvorených pokladničných dokladov (weekly and monthly), vývoj tržieb v eurách, tržby/doklady by self-governing region, tržby/doklady by SK NACE2 industry code, count of registered online (ORP) and virtual (VRP) cash registers. This is till-level turnover and transaction-count evidence for the whole SK retail/HORECA economy, published by the tax authority rather than NBS, and is the natural denominator against which card/POS transaction volumes can be benchmarked.
candidates.access_status: public, free, open licence, no registration observed
candidates.legal_status: explicitly published as open data for repeated free re-use (commercial and non-commercial)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled scrape of the category page to enumerate dataset landing pages, then download the XLSX attachments (weekly/monthly cadence); normalise into a time series keyed by period + region + NACE. Check whether an OData/CKAN-style endpoint exists at the portal root before falling back to file scraping.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on seed query + direct fetch of the category page
queries_used: Finančná správa eKasa štatistiky pokladnice tržby
financnasprava.sk otvorené dáta open data index daňovej spoľahlivosti eKasa datasety

negative_findings.description: No eKasa dataset was found that splits recorded turnover or receipts by tender type (hotovosť vs. platobná karta / bezhotovostne). The ODFS eKasa category exposes turnover and receipt counts by period, region and SK NACE2, plus register counts — but not payment method.
negative_findings.result_summary: 10 eKasa datasets enumerated on the ODFS category page; none of the titles or descriptions references payment method, card, or cash tender split.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This is the cell's headline hypothesis — eKasa as the hard cash-vs-card-at-the-till evidence source. The transactional data exists inside the system (receipts carry the payment method) but is not published, so cash share must be inferred indirectly (eKasa turnover as denominator against NBS card-acquiring volumes) or requested via an infožiadosť under the freedom-of-information act.

negative_findings.description: No ATM-related statistics were found from any institution in this cell (ŠÚ SR, MF SR, Finančná správa, NKÚ). Searches on cash/ATM terms returned only central-bank-adjacent or commercial material.
negative_findings.result_summary: Zero candidates for ATM network, ATM withdrawal volumes or cash-in-transit from fiscal/statistical bodies.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that ATM data for SK is genuinely NBS/ECB territory and that this cell should not be relied on for it; workstream coverage of ATM statistics must come from the central-bank cell.

negative_findings.description: SLOVSTAT, named in the cell definition, is retired: ŠÚ SR suspended its data updates from 1 November 2017 and closed access on 31 October 2018; content moved to DATAcube, which is itself now being migrated to STATdata (created 2024).

negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any collection design or historical citation pointing at SLOVSTAT will fail; and a DATAcube-only pipeline will silently miss new cubes created only in STATdata during the migration.

brief: Slovakia's non-central-bank fiscal and statistical bodies form an unusually rich, fully open source landscape for payments intelligence, anchored by two systems: the Financial Administration's ODFS open-data portal, which publishes ~10 recurring eKasa datasets (receipt counts weekly/monthly, turnover in EUR, and both split by self-governing region and SK NACE2 industry code, plus counts of registered online and virtual cash registers), and the Statistical Office's DATAcube database with a JSON-stat/CSV API at data.statistics.sk covering retail and internal-trade turnover, household surveys and ICT/e-commerce use. The critical limitation is that eKasa aggregates are not broken down by tender type, so cash-versus-card at the till must be inferred by using eKasa turnover as a denominator against card-acquiring volumes, or obtained through a freedom-of-information request — the data exists inside the system but is unpublished. A secondary analytical and oversight layer (IFP and ÚHP at MF SR on the VAT gap and tax-collection efficiency, the MF SR cash-payment-limit page, NKÚ's ongoing-audit register and budget opinions, and NR SR explanatory memoranda) supplies interpretation, policy direction and forward-looking impact estimates, with Act No. 384/2025 Z. z. on evidencia tržieb, effective 1 January 2026, as the live regulatory event to watch. Two structural risks for any pipeline: SLOVSTAT is retired and DATAcube is migrating to STATdata, and everything of substance is Slovak-language and distributed as XLSX or PDF rather than via a stable API.
